Subject: Request: selective log tombstoning evidence for SOC 2 / CAIQ mapping

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SOC 2 and CAIQ review for our upcoming integration, we need clarity and evidence for Redwood's handling of tenant-scoped log retention and targeted deletions (what we call "selective tombstoning"). Specifically Evexis is evaluating whether we can rely on Redwood to: 1) delete user-content artifacts on request while retaining aggregated telemetry for observability, and 2) demonstrate that retained telemetry cannot be reconstructed to re-create deleted content.

Could you provide the following artifacts / answers?:
- A retention matrix that maps artifact type (API request logs, KV cache traces, streaming transcript shards, embeddings, audit trails) to canonical retention windows and deletion paths (soft delete / hard wipe / tombstone)
- A sanitized sample of logs showing the deletion workflow for a single tenant (with tenant id redacted) and an explanation of what is retained vs permanently purged
- For items you mark as "tombstoned" (retained but non-reconstructible), a short technical note describing the transform/cryptographic guarantees (e.g. irreversible hashing, irreversible truncation) and the control owner/team that enforces it
- CAIQ/SIG control mapping for data disposition (where applicable) and any SOC 2 artifact references we can attach to our audit folder
- Proof-of-delete timeline example (audit log entries, S3 lifecycle job ids, or equivalent) for a sample deletion request

We are happy to receive sanitized artifacts via a secure share link (we can provide a ShareFile account if you prefer) or a Redwood-provided secure drive. If there's a better way to scope this to avoid disclosing PII, please advise.

Appreciate a reply with proposed timeline. We ideally need evidence to attach to our SOC audit by the end of next week (2026-05-21).

Best,
Eve Zhang
Security & Privacy, Evexis Therapeutics
security@evexis.com

Hi Eve / Gabe —

Thanks again for the request and the context. Attached (secure link below) is our initial bundle addressing the items you listed: retention_matrix.csv (maps artifact types to canonical retention and deletion path), sample_sanitized_logs.txt (single-tenant walkthrough with synthetic id), and evidence_manifest.pdf (what each artifact proves and references to SOC 2 control IDs).

High-level summary:
- We support targeted deletions for customer-scoped content. Where we retain telemetry for operational observability we apply irreversible transforms to ensure the retained blob is non-reconstructible. For embeddings we use one-way salt+hash with per-tenant salts and we remove the raw k/v cache entries on delete; for streaming transcript shards we retain only aggregate token counts and anonymized latency buckets.
- The retention matrix in the bundle maps these behaviors to CAIQ / SIG disposition control families and references the indicative SOC 2 artifacts (control owner and sample evidence file ids).
- The sanitized sample includes inline comments where fields were redacted and the SIEM export ids for the deletion event.
